candidates.title: VideoJSON: A Minimal Harness Beats Purpose-Built Memory for Ultra-Long Video Understanding
candidates.content: Answering questions over days or weeks of video requires searching for scattered clues across long timelines. Existing video agents rely on complex memory graphs and fixed retrieval pipelines, which restrict how the agent can search. We propose VideoJSON, a minimal harness for ultra-long video understanding that keeps the memory simple and lets a coding agent write its own search programs. During indexing, a vision-language model turns each minute of video into a single JSON record containing a dense caption and structured fields such as events, entities, places, and speech transcripts. At query time, the agent writes Python or Bash programs in a sandboxed container to filter, link, and read these records over multiple steps, without task-specific training or raw video access. On four ultra-long video benchmarks, VideoJSON with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash outperforms MAGIC-Video by 7.0, 20.0, and 24.75 points on EgoLifeQA, Ego-R1-Bench, and MM-Lifelong Week, and beats the best prior EgoMemReason score by 12.6 points. Across four policy models of increasing capability, VideoJSON's average score rises by up to 11.58 points over the weakest model, compared with at most 5.50 points for MAGIC-V

candidates.title: Self-Supervised Dataset Distillation via Mutual Information Maximization
candidates.content: Dataset distillation (DD) aims to compress a large dataset into a small synthetic one that remains effective for training neural networks. Despite its success in supervised learning, DD remains underexplored in self-supervised learning (SSL), where distilled data must preserve the information needed to learn representations that remain consistent across augmentations. To bridge this gap, we introduce Mutual Information Prototype Alignment (MIPA), an efficient SSL dataset distillation approach that optimizes synthetic images to preserve augmentation-invariant information. Specifically, MIPA treats synthetic images as learnable prototypes and uses a frozen encoder to assign real samples to them based on feature similarity. A synthetic dataset that preserves such augmentation invariance should yield stable prototype assignments across multiple augmented views of the same real image. MIPA encourages this by maximizing mutual information between cross-view assignments while avoiding trivial solutions in which all real samples are assigned to only a few synthetic prototypes. candidates.title: Measuring and Teaching Language Model Agents to Act on Delayed Consequences
candidates.content: Language model agents are increasingly asked to run ongoing multi-day operations rather than finish isolated single-turn tasks. In daily operations, today's choices reshape later observations and cash constraints because empty shelves hide lost walk-in demand, short-shipped customers quietly shrink future orders weeks later, and emergency buying drains working capital. We introduce SMB Bench, a calibrated 90-day wholesale simulator with 18 causally paired tasks and an 859-run frontier trace dataset, to ask what experience and learning signal make an agent better at noticing, attributing, and acting on the delayed consequences of its own decisions in unseen businesses. Across 16 frontier models, only 3 outperform a fixed buying rule; models often record a relevant diagnosis in their notes without changing later purchases in time, showing that diagnosing a problem, changing behavior, and improving a business are separate achievements. candidates.title: Rituximab Maintenance in Eosinophilic Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis
candidates.content: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is the rarest of the antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)–associated vasculitides and is defined clinically by asthma, eosinophilia, chronic rhinosinusitis, pulmonary infiltrates, and necrotizing vasculitis and eosinophil-rich granulomatous inflammation involving a variety of organ systems. Only 30% to 40% of patients are ANCA positive (usually against myeloperoxidase), and ANCA status often correlates with distinct but overlapping clinical patterns. Historically, glucocorticoids have been the mainstay of EGPA treatment; although the treatment has never been tested adequately prospectively, patients with organ- or life-threatening disease typically receive remission induction with high-dose glucocorticoids plus cyclophosphamide or, in select cases, rituximab. Patients without organ-threatening manifestations have been treated with glucocorticoids alone or in combination with steroid-sparing agents such as azathioprine, methotrexate, or mycophenolate. candidates.title: New Drug Technologies and Their Histories
candidates.content: Here’s a look at how long it can take for new drug technologies to actually make it to the clinic and to FDA approval - including why it takes as long as it does and how that might be sped up. Four techniques get a close look and comparison: fragment-based drug discovery (FBDD), DNA-encoded libraries DEL), aptamers, and targeted protein degradation. I have written posts about all of these over the years (and personally done work on some of them as well!) It’s interesting to note the timelines. For fragments, the first big demonstration was in 1996 and 15 years later the first drug discovered through fragment-based techniques was approved by the FDA. For DEL, the original proof-of-concept was probably around 2004, but to date (as far as this paper’s author has been able to find out) no drugs have been approved that came up by this route, which I hadn’t realized (this could change fairly soon, it should be noted). As for aptamers, their POC came back in 1992 and the first FDA approval in 2004, although there have been only two drugs that have made it that far in over thirty years. And finally, PROTAC degraders showed POC in 2001, and the first drug of this kind was approved this year

candidates.title: Chemotherapy Actually Helps Immunotherapy in Cancer
candidates.content: This paper’s conclusions seem well worth knowing: the authors are looking at the intersection of what are usually considered two rather different forms of cancer treatment (therapeutic vaccines to mobilize the immune system and the more classic chemotherapy approaches). The paper notes that tests of such vaccines often take place in patients who are themselves receiving chemotherapy, and in fact some beneficial interactions have been seen. So they tested some viral-vector vaccines in combination with common chemotherapy (carboplatin plus paclitaxel, “CarboTaxol”) in mice. The added chemotherapy was definitely beneficial compared to the therapeutic vaccine. Previous studies had shown myeloid depletion with the chemotherapy which seemed to aid later vaccine performance, but in this case they were given simultaneously. A close look at the T cells and myeloid cells here suggests that myeloid depletion is indeed part of the story, but not all of it - there are other mechanisms at work that need to be figured out. candidates.content: by Dante G. Calise, Madeline L. Michaelis, Jin Woo Bok, Zhili Chen, Joshua J. Coon, Anna Huttenlocher, Benjamin J. Chadwick, Nancy P. Keller Aspergillus fumigatus is a major opportunistic fungal pathogen whose ability to maintain hyphal integrity and withstand host defenses is critical for virulence. Septal pores, which connect hyphal compartments, are dynamically regulated to preserve cellular integrity under stress, yet the molecular components governing this process remain incompletely defined. Deletion of sppA resulted in defective septal organization and increased susceptibility to hyphal damage. candidates.title: RNA fine-tunes KAT5 activity to shape chromatin acetylation during active transcription
candidates.content: Abstract KAT5 is a prominent histone acetyltransferase that deposits acetylation on histone H4 to regulate transcription, genome stability, and cell fate decisions. Although the chromatin recruitment of KAT5 and its associated NuA4/TIP60 complex is well characterized, the molecular mechanisms that regulate its catalytic activity are still largely unknown. Here, we identify RNA as a direct and reversible modulator of KAT5 activity. Using single-end enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation sequencing (seCLIP-seq), we find that KAT5 binds RNA in cells with a strong preference for GC-rich mRNA sequences enriched near transcription start sites. Unexpectedly, loss of KAT5–RNA interactions during acute transcriptional inhibition triggers rapid and pronounced promoter hyperacetylation. Biochemical and structural analyses suggest that RNA engages an RNA-sensing autoinhibitory region within the HAT domain, sterically blocking substrate access to the catalytic pocket and thereby suppressing KAT5 acetyltransferase activity. candidates.title: Nicking Loop™: streamlined circular DNA libraries for precise targeted sequencing and universal NGS read-out
candidates.content: Abstract Circular single-stranded DNA (CssDNA) offers unique advantages for molecular diagnostics and next-generation sequencing (NGS) due to its nuclease degradation resistance and compatibility with rolling circle amplification. CssDNA is used with several modern NGS platforms, but many library preparation workflows require a conversion step involving splinting and an enzymatic treatment, adding workflow complexity. This study introduces Nicking Loop™, a targeted library preparation method that converts single- and double-stranded DNA into CssDNA, enabling direct circular sequencing and controlled linear amplification that can be repeated over multiple generations. The method demonstrated improved preservation of variant allele frequencies across three amplification generations compared to PCR, which is particularly relevant for detection of low-abundance variants. candidates.title: Vintage Mistakes
candidates.content: This Nature article dives into a topic that’s always been divisive and is becoming more so all the time: what happens when a paper gets retracted? Does its full text still stay up on the journal website and other archives? Is it still searchable (and still fodder for AI/ML mining)? Can it still be cited? OK, now let’s go a step further. What if that paper has been in the literature for years when it turns out to be invalid? You have all those questions, and you can add some more: what about the citations that it has accumulated? The times it has been mentioned in review articles? Or how such publications and their faked data and conclusions can resurface using modern database searches? As many will have had cause to appreciate, just getting current bullshit retracted is already hard enough - now imagine trying to so something about it when everyone involved is dead. The article mentions the specific example of Vishwa Jit Gupta, who published hundreds of fraudulent papers about Himalayan fossils and geology in the 1960s, 70s, and 80s. candidates.title: A shared interbacterial membrane underlies mycobacterial cording
candidates.content: Cording is a century-old mycobacterial virulence trait. CryoET and light microscopy reveal that incomplete cell separation during division generates a shared interbacterial membrane. candidates.title: PixelOne: From Options to Pixels in a Single Forward for GUI Grounding
candidates.content: GUI grounding requires precise clicks at low latency. Recent models such as GUI-Decisions and GUI-Swift predict coordinates in one forward pass using fixed global bins with local refinement. However, screenshot downsampling removes detail needed to locate small controls, while fixed bins cover larger pixel ranges at higher resolutions. We introduce PixelOne, which transfers spatial knowledge from a search teacher to a student that predicts clicks directly from screenshots at native resolution. The teacher uses VideoJEV's text-option scorer to select rows and columns and progressively zoom into candidate regions. The student inherits the teacher's parameters and matches its distributions over explored regions through spatial distillation alongside box supervision. At inference, the same decision head selects a visual token, and a lightweight pixel head predicts the click within it, all in one forward pass. A click-aligned loss encourages pixels inside the target box to score above those outside. Across four benchmarks, PixelOne-Pro-35B-A3B achieves 83.8% mean accuracy, the highest among the evaluated single-forward grounders, with a mean latency of 0.43 s per target.
